candidates.original_title: Action observation modulates auditory perception of the consequence of others’ actions
candidates.description: Self-initiated auditory action-effects are perceived as less intense than externally generated or observed auditory action-effects, indicating sensory attenuation.
candidates.citation_sentence: The sensory attenuation task was a modification of paradigms previously used to investigate sensory attenuation of auditory action-effects [37], [38].
candidates.notes: The paper explicitly states that it replicated previously reported perceptual differences, but sensory attenuation was significant only in the TB-SA order and not overall, so the outcome is inconclusive. candidates.original_title: Temporal binding of action and effect in interval reproduction
candidates.description: The perceived interval between a voluntary action and its sensory effect is shorter than the interval between externally generated events, producing temporal binding.
candidates.citation_sentence: By contrast, studies which measure the perception of temporal intervals more directly (via numerical estimates or asking participants to reproduce the interval between two events) have reported temporal binding at much longer intervals [24],[25].
candidates.notes: The replication found the classic temporal binding effect and describes it as such. The paper cites the original using numbered references rather than author-year citations. [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
